correctness.rationale: The definitions and quantifiers are explicit. Minimality for total side size below six follows from the bound that a two-element side has only three nonempty distinct neighborhoods, together with direct classification of the 2-by-2 and 2-by-3 cases and transposes. The two 3-by-3 witnesses are visibly bi-twin-free, both dual complexes are full 2-simplices because each relation has a universal row and column, and nonisomorphism follows from preserved row-degree multisets. The exhaustive verifier independently enumerates all 512 matrices, obtains 174 labeled bi-twin-free matrices, eight row/column-permutation classes, seven dual-Dowker signatures, and a unique size-two collision. No infinite claim rests on finite experimentation.

value.rationale: The question is structurally motivated by the exact information loss of the Dowker construction: once trivial duplicate neighborhoods and isolated vertices are removed, it is natural to ask whether retaining both dual complexes recovers the relation. The result gives the sharp smallest negative answer, a complete census at that boundary, and a canonical pair of witnesses. This directly clarifies why weights/cosheaf or relation-level constructions carry genuinely more information than merely storing both dual complexes; it is not an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of a known table.
